## Cause

The regression is the most recent commit, `4d99828` "Drop indexes with no recorded reads (Q3 storage review)".

The duplicate-payment race was closed in `5940039` with two halves:
1. `PaymentService.create` doing the existence check inside the transaction (`PaymentService.java:29`), and
2. a unique index `ux_payment_idempotency_key` on `payment(idempotency_key)` (`V2__payment_unique_index.sql`).

Half 1 alone is not sufficient — under read-committed, two concurrent transactions (or two app instances) both see `existsByIdempotencyKey == false` and both insert. The index was the actual guarantee; the application check is only an optimisation.

`V3__drop_unused_indexes.sql` dropped that index because `pg_stat_user_indexes` reported zero reads on it. It reports zero reads precisely because it's a uniqueness constraint, not a lookup path — nothing ever scans it. Dropping it reopened the exact race `5940039` fixed. The Java side is untouched and still correct; only the DB constraint disappeared.

## Fix

`src/main/resources/db/migration/V4__restore_payment_idempotency_index.sql` recreates the index, with a comment explaining why index-usage tooling will always report it as unused so the next storage review doesn't drop it a third time. I also refreshed the now-stale `V2__...` references in the `PaymentService` and `Payment` comments to point at the current migration.

I did not edit `V3`, since it has already been applied in production and changing it would break migration checksums.

`mvn -o test` passes (the existing suite is one arithmetic test; it doesn't exercise this path).

## Before deploying

- **Reconcile existing duplicates first.** `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` will fail if any duplicate `idempotency_key` rows exist, and by definition some do — that's the incident. Find and resolve them before running V4:
  ```sql
  SELECT idempotency_key, count(*), array_agg(id)
  FROM payment GROUP BY idempotency_key HAVING count(*) > 1;
  ```
- **Consider `CONCURRENTLY`** if the `payment` table is large enough that a table-level lock during index build isn't acceptable; that requires running the statement outside a transaction.

## One thing I left alone, deliberately

With the index restored, the loser of a race gets a `DataIntegrityViolationException` out of `create` rather than the existing payment — a 500 to that caller, though no double charge, and a client retry with the same key then returns the existing row. That matches the design `5940039` describes ("the index alone turns a duplicate into an exception"). Converting it into a clean return needs the catch to sit outside the transaction boundary — the transaction is already doomed by the time the constraint fires — which means splitting the insert into a separate bean. That's a real change to transaction structure and adjacent to the ask, so I didn't fold it into a production hotfix. Happy to do it as a follow-up.
